q: Contoso is shipping 200 TPM 2.0-equipped shared-floor tablets to a depot. Staff will only unbox and power them on. Nobody signs in during setup, and each tablet must end up joined to Microsoft Entra ID with no primary user. Which Autopilot approach fits?
opts: A user-driven profile with Microsoft Entra join, assigned to the depot staff's user group
An Autopilot device preparation policy assigned to the depot staff's user group
A pre-provisioned deployment that uses a user-driven profile, run by the depot staff
A self-deploying profile, assigned to the registered devices through a device group
why: A self-deploying profile authenticates the device with its TPM 2.0 attestation, needs no user credentials, and leaves the device with no primary user, so it fits a power-on-only setup. A user-driven profile, with or without pre-provisioning, still ends with a person signing in with their own credentials, which also makes them the primary user. Device preparation policies target users and are likewise user-driven, so someone would still have to sign in.

q: New hires will set up their own laptops at home over slow broadband. At first sign-in, Autopilot spends over an hour on the Enrollment Status Page installing 12 required device apps. The laptops pass through a reseller first and support TPM 2.0 attestation. IT wants the end user's wait cut without changing which apps are required. What should IT do?
opts: Switch the deployment profile to self-deploying so provisioning runs unattended without the end user present at the device
Raise the Enrollment Status Page timeout so the installs have longer to finish on the home connection
Use pre-provisioning (white glove) so the device-targeted apps and policies are installed before the laptops ship
Change the 12 apps from Required to Available so users install them later from the Company Portal
why: Pre-provisioning moves the device phase, including device-targeted apps and policies, into a technician phase that the reseller completes before shipping, so the new hire only sits through the short user phase. A self-deploying profile removes the user sign-in but would still run every install over the hire's slow connection, and a user-affiliated shipment does not suit it. A longer timeout only prevents a timeout failure, it does not shorten the wait, and making the apps Available changes the requirement the scenario says to keep.

q: A hybrid Microsoft Entra joined fleet is co-managed, with every workload slider still set to Configuration Manager. The company now wants these devices managed by Windows Autopatch. Which change is required before the devices qualify?
opts: Uninstall the Configuration Manager client from the devices so that Intune becomes the management authority
Move the Windows Update policies, Device configuration, and Office Click-to-Run apps workloads to Intune or Pilot Intune
Move the Compliance policies workload to Intune, because compliance status is what Autopatch evaluates first
Convert the devices from hybrid Microsoft Entra joined to Microsoft Entra joined and remove their AD computer accounts
why: For co-managed devices, Autopatch needs Intune to be authoritative for the workloads that control updates, device configuration, and Microsoft 365 Apps, so those three sliders must be at Pilot Intune or Intune. Compliance policies is a different workload that Autopatch does not depend on. Removing the Configuration Manager client is unnecessary because co-managed devices are supported, and hybrid Entra join is already an eligible join state.

q: A 24/7 operations center complains that monthly patching forces restarts. An admin enables Hotpatch for its eligible Windows devices and tells the team there will be no more restarts. Which statement sets accurate expectations?
opts: Devices stay on one baseline and skip cumulative updates until the next feature update arrives
Monthly restarts still happen, but they are held back until the user next signs out of the device
Most monthly security fixes apply in memory without a restart, but periodic baseline updates still restart the device
Restarts are removed for security, driver, and feature updates that arrive through the same update ring and schedule
why: Hotpatch applies a subset of security fixes to the running OS in memory, which removes the restart in most months, but not every fix can be applied that way, so devices periodically land on a baseline cumulative update that does restart. Hotpatch does not cover driver or feature updates. It does not merely postpone the restart, and it does not let a device skip cumulative updates altogether.

q: A distribution center has 90 employees on three non-overlapping 8-hour shifts, about 30 per shift. Each worker should get a Windows 365 Cloud PC at the start of their shift, and the company wants to buy the fewest licenses that still work. Which licensing should it buy?
opts: Windows 365 Enterprise licenses for all 90 named employees, one per person
Windows 365 Frontline (now Windows 365 Flex) licenses sized for the 30 workers connected at any one time
Windows 365 Enterprise licenses for 30 users, reassigned between shifts as workers rotate
Windows 365 Frontline (now Windows 365 Flex) licenses for all 90 named employees, one per person
why: Frontline (renamed Windows 365 Flex in 2026, with licensing unchanged) is licensed by the number of Cloud PCs in use at the same time, not by named user, so 30 Frontline licenses can serve shift workers who never overlap. Enterprise is one license per named user, so buying it for 90 people is the most expensive route. Frontline licenses for all 90 people ignore the concurrency model and waste the saving, and reassigning Enterprise licenses between shifts would repeatedly deprovision the Cloud PCs instead of giving each worker a persistent one.

q: Windows 11 devices sit in an update ring with a 0-day feature update deferral. IT wants them to stay on version 25H2 even after 26H2 is released, while still receiving monthly security updates on the ring's schedule. What should IT assign?
opts: A change to the existing ring that raises its feature update deferral to the 365-day maximum
An expedited quality update policy that targets the 25H2 release for these devices
A pause on the update ring until the 26H2 release has been validated in the pilot group
A feature update deployment profile that targets 25H2, keeping the ring for quality updates
why: A feature update deployment profile pins the group to a target version, so the devices stay on 25H2 until the profile is changed or removed, while the ring keeps governing monthly quality updates. A deferral only delays the upgrade, so devices move to 26H2 once the 365 days elapse. A pause is temporary and ends automatically after a limited period, and an expedited policy accelerates quality updates and has no say over the feature version.

q: A co-managed, hybrid-joined fleet is run by Configuration Manager. IT wants Intune to take over only Windows Update policies, first for 20 pilot devices and later for everyone, without touching other workloads. What should IT configure?
opts: Enable tenant attach and run the update installation action from the cloud console on the 20 devices
Move every workload slider to Pilot Intune and rely on the pilot collection to limit which workloads apply
Set the Windows Update policies slider to Pilot Intune and assign a pilot collection holding those 20 devices
Set the Windows Update policies slider to Intune and exclude the other devices with an assignment filter
why: Each workload slider has a Pilot Intune position that applies only to the devices in that workload's pilot collection, so one workload can be staged on 20 devices and later moved to Intune for everyone. Setting the slider to Intune moves the whole fleet at once, and assignment filters live in Intune rather than in the Configuration Manager slider. Moving every workload to Pilot Intune touches workloads the scenario says to leave alone, and tenant attach runs one-off actions without changing which tool is authoritative.

q: The Group Policy setting for automatic MDM enrollment is applied to hybrid Microsoft Entra joined Windows 11 PCs, yet none of them appear in Intune. The users are licensed. What should the admin check first?
opts: That the Intune Connector for Active Directory is installed on a domain-joined server
That the MDM user scope in Microsoft Entra ID includes the users who sign in to those PCs
That an Autopilot deployment profile is assigned to the PCs, since it triggers enrollment
That a compliance policy is assigned to the PCs so that Intune can recognize them
why: Automatic enrollment through Group Policy still depends on the MDM user scope in Microsoft Entra ID, so users outside that scope never enroll even though the policy applies and the PCs are hybrid joined. Autopilot is a provisioning path for new or reset devices, not a prerequisite for GPO enrollment. A compliance policy is assigned after a device exists in Intune, and the Intune Connector for Active Directory only supports Autopilot hybrid join, where it creates the computer object.

q: A specific laptop model is not being offered the latest Windows feature update through its update ring, even though every configured deferral period has already elapsed. What is the most likely explanation?
opts: The laptops are failing their compliance policy, and noncompliant devices are excluded from feature update rollout
A driver update policy set to manual approval is also holding back feature updates for the same devices
A safeguard hold, applied by Microsoft after detecting a known compatibility issue with that hardware, is blocking the update
The ring's feature deferral counts from each device's enrollment date, not the release date, so it has not elapsed yet
why: A safeguard hold is applied automatically by Microsoft when it detects a known compatibility problem for a device or hardware and driver combination, and it blocks that feature update until Microsoft lifts it or an admin deliberately opts out of safeguard holds. Deferral days count from the release date, so the stem's elapsed deferrals rule out a timing cause. Compliance status does not gate feature update offers, and a driver update policy governs drivers only.

q: When a feature update deployment profile targets devices that also receive an update ring, the ring's feature update deferral no longer delays the feature update for those devices.
opts: True
False
why: This sounds wrong because the deferral is still configured in the ring, but the deployment profile takes precedence over the ring's feature deferral for its devices. The ring continues to govern their quality updates.

q: Contoso is registering devices with Windows Autopatch. Assuming licensing requirements are met, which of these devices is eligible?
opts: A Windows 11 PC joined to on-premises AD and managed through the Configuration Manager client
A Windows 11 laptop that is Microsoft Entra joined and enrolled in Intune
A personal Windows 11 laptop that is Microsoft Entra registered, with the user's work account added
An iPad enrolled in Intune through Automated Device Enrollment
why: Autopatch manages Windows devices that are Microsoft Entra joined or hybrid joined and already managed by Intune. A device that is merely Entra registered is a personal-device state outside that requirement, a PC managed only by Configuration Manager has neither an Entra join nor Intune management, and Autopatch does not manage iPads.

q: A self-deploying Autopilot profile can hybrid Microsoft Entra join a device, provided the Intune Connector for Active Directory is installed.
opts: True
False
why: Self-deploying profiles support Microsoft Entra join only. Hybrid join through Autopilot needs a user-driven profile, with the Intune Connector for Active Directory creating the on-premises computer object.

q: A co-managed device keeps its Configuration Manager client installed even after every co-management workload slider has been moved to Intune.
opts: True
False
why: Workload sliders only change which tool is authoritative for each workload. They do not remove the Configuration Manager client, which stays on the device until it is retired separately.

q: Which two statements about Windows Autopilot deployment profile types are correct? (Choose two.)
opts: A self-deploying profile supports Microsoft Entra join but not hybrid Entra join
A user-driven profile can run to completion without any user signing in
A self-deploying profile makes the first person who signs in the device's primary user
Pre-provisioning removes the need for an Enrollment Status Page during the technician phase
A pre-provisioned deployment can use either a user-driven or a self-deploying profile type
why: Self-deploying profiles support Microsoft Entra join only, and pre-provisioning can be combined with either user-driven or self-deploying profile types. A user-driven profile cannot finish without a user's credentials, a self-deploying device has no user affiliation and so no primary user, and the Enrollment Status Page is exactly what tracks progress during the technician phase.

q: Which two statements about Windows Autopatch and Hotpatch are accurate? (Choose two.)
opts: A hotpatch builds on a current baseline, so a device that fell behind gets a full update with a restart
Hotpatch removes restarts for feature updates delivered through the same deployment ring as security updates
Autopatch manages updates for third-party applications such as Chrome and Adobe Reader as part of its default rings
Autopatch enrollment excludes Microsoft Entra joined devices and accepts hybrid joined ones as the supported state
Autopatch can update Microsoft 365 Apps and Microsoft Edge in addition to Windows quality updates
why: Autopatch covers Windows quality updates, drivers and firmware, Microsoft 365 Apps, and Edge, and a hotpatch is a delta on a current baseline, so a device that fell behind receives the full cumulative update with a restart. Autopatch does not manage third-party apps, hotpatching applies to security updates rather than feature updates, and Entra joined devices are eligible alongside hybrid joined ones.

q: New corporate laptops enroll through the Company Portal rather than Autopilot. IT wants users to pick 'Kiosk' or 'Executive' during enrollment, and a dynamic device group to follow that choice. Which device attribute should the group's membership rule use?
opts: The Autopilot group tag property
The device ownership property
The device category property
The scope tag assigned to the device
why: Device category is the label a user can be prompted to choose at enrollment, and it can be used in dynamic group rules. A group tag exists only on Autopilot registrations, so laptops enrolled through the Company Portal have none. Ownership records corporate versus personal, not purpose, and a scope tag limits which admins can see an object and is not an attribute a dynamic group can filter on.

q: Laptops were registered for Autopilot with the group tag 'Kiosk'. IT needs a dynamic Microsoft Entra device group that contains only those devices, so a deployment profile can be assigned to it. Which membership rule should be used?
opts: (device.devicePhysicalIds -any (_ -contains "[ZTDId]"))
(device.deviceCategory -eq "Kiosk")
(device.devicePhysicalIds -any (_ -eq "[PurchaseOrderId]:Kiosk"))
(device.devicePhysicalIds -any (_ -eq "[OrderID]:Kiosk"))
why: An Autopilot group tag is stored in the device's physical IDs with the OrderID prefix, so matching [OrderID]:Kiosk selects exactly the tagged devices. The ZTDId rule matches every Autopilot-registered device regardless of tag. PurchaseOrderId matches a different registration attribute, and device category is the label set at enrollment, not something Autopilot registration populates.

q: A zero-day fix was released today. Most update rings defer quality updates seven days. Security needs 40 high-risk laptops patched immediately, even outside active hours, without editing any existing ring. What should the admin create?
opts: A change to the existing rings that lowers quality update deferral to zero days for every device
A feature update deployment profile for the 40 laptops that targets the newest Windows version
A driver update policy set to automatic approval for the 40 laptops
An expedited quality update policy for that release, assigned to the 40 laptops
why: An expedited quality update policy pushes an already-released fix to a targeted group right away, bypassing the ring's deferral and active hours, and leaves every existing ring untouched. A feature update profile governs the Windows version, not a monthly security fix, and a driver update policy governs drivers. Lowering deferral on the existing rings breaks the no-edit constraint and would also pull the fix forward for every other device.

q: A new OEM camera driver is breaking video calls on one laptop model. IT wants to stop that one driver from installing on those laptops while other approved drivers keep installing. Which approach fits?
opts: Turn off driver delivery in the update ring so no drivers install on any device in it
Create a safeguard hold for that driver so Intune blocks it on the affected laptops
Assign an expedited quality update that replaces the driver with the previous version
Use a driver update policy and withhold or pause approval for that one driver
why: A Windows driver update policy lets an admin control drivers individually, either by approving drivers one by one or by pausing a specific driver, so the bad driver is held back while others continue. Turning off driver delivery in the ring blocks all drivers, which the scenario does not want. An expedited quality update does not roll back drivers, and safeguard holds are applied by Microsoft rather than configured by an administrator.

q: Which two statements about feature update deployment profiles and expedited quality updates are accurate? (Choose two.)
opts: A feature update deployment profile overrides the feature update deferral of a ring assigned to the same devices
An expedited quality update can install and restart a device outside its ring's deferral and active hours
Expedited quality updates are available only for devices enrolled in Windows Autopatch
An expedited update deployment can also pin devices to a specific Windows feature version instead of a fix
A feature update deployment profile replaces the quality update deferral of the ring assigned to the same devices
why: A feature update deployment profile overrides the ring's feature deferral for its devices, and an expedited quality update is built to push an urgent fix past normal deferral and active hours. Expediting concerns quality updates and cannot pin a feature version, the profile leaves the ring's quality deferral in charge, and expediting is an Intune policy that does not require Autopatch.

q: A quality update broke a line-of-business app and reached the entire broad ring, because the pilot ring held only five IT laptops that never run that app. Which design change would have caught the problem before the broad ring received the update?
opts: Raise the pilot ring's quality update deferral to 30 days so it receives updates after the broad ring does
Replace the update rings with a feature update deployment profile assigned to the whole fleet of devices
Make the earliest ring a representative sample of departments and apps, with a short deferral before later rings
Pause quality updates fleet-wide each month until IT finishes testing the line-of-business apps in a lab
why: Staged rings only protect the fleet if the early ring is representative, so a small cross-section of departments and app sets, with a short deferral ahead of the larger rings, surfaces a regression before the broad population gets it. Deferring the pilot ring behind the broad ring defeats its purpose. A feature update profile does not stage monthly quality updates, and pausing the whole fleet delays security fixes for everyone and is only a temporary measure.

q: A device is enrolled in Autopatch and eligible for Hotpatch, but it has skipped its baseline cumulative update for over four months. What is likely to happen the next time a hotpatch is released?
opts: The device receives the full cumulative update with a restart, since a hotpatch applies only on a current baseline
Autopatch removes the device from its deployment ring until a baseline update is installed manually by an admin
The device is blocked from quality updates until an admin resets its Hotpatch enrollment in the admin center
The hotpatch installs in memory as normal, since hotpatches do not depend on any earlier baseline update on the device
why: A hotpatch is a delta that applies on top of a recent baseline cumulative update, so a device that has fallen behind is offered the full cumulative update, with its restart, to get back on the baseline. The hotpatch cannot install on an out-of-date baseline, Autopatch does not drop the device from its ring, and there is no admin step to reset Hotpatch enrollment before updates resume.

q: A device is hybrid Entra joined, domain-joined, and already has the Configuration Manager client installed, but it is not yet enrolled in Intune. GPO-based automatic MDM enrollment is configured tenant-wide. An administrator also enables co-management on this same device. What is the resulting state?
opts: The device cannot be both Intune-enrolled and Configuration Manager-managed, so co-management fails until the Configuration Manager client is uninstalled
The device becomes Intune-enrolled, but Intune is authoritative only for workloads whose sliders were moved; the rest stay with Configuration Manager
GPO-based automatic enrollment is blocked on devices that already have the Configuration Manager client installed
Intune becomes authoritative for every workload the moment enrollment completes, whatever the slider positions are
why: GPO-based enrollment works on a hybrid joined device regardless of the Configuration Manager client, and co-management exists precisely so that one device can be Intune-enrolled and ConfigMgr-managed at once, with each workload slider deciding which tool is authoritative for that workload. Enrollment alone does not shift any workload, the client does not have to be removed, and its presence does not block automatic enrollment.

q: A branch office has 150 PCs on a slow WAN link that all download the same large updates. Which two statements about using Delivery Optimization to ease the load are accurate? (Choose two.)
opts: HTTP-only mode lets branch devices peer over the local network while still falling back to Microsoft
Each branch needs a Configuration Manager distribution point before its devices can peer with one another
LAN download mode limits peering to devices on the local network, keeping shared content inside the branch
Peers can share Win32 app content deployed through Intune, not just Windows updates
Delivery Optimization applies to Windows quality updates only, so feature updates and apps still download individually
why: Delivery Optimization also serves Win32 and Microsoft Store app content, and LAN mode keeps peering on the local network, which is why it suits a branch with a constrained WAN link. No Configuration Manager distribution point is needed for peering. It is not limited to quality updates, and HTTP-only mode disables peering altogether, so every device would download from Microsoft individually.

q: Which two configurations are required for a user-driven Windows Autopilot deployment that must hybrid Microsoft Entra join new laptops? (Choose two.)
opts: A self-deploying Autopilot profile with the hybrid join option selected
The Intune Connector for Active Directory installed on a domain-joined server
A Microsoft Entra registered record created in advance for each laptop
A Domain Join configuration profile that names the domain and the target OU
An Autopilot device preparation policy assigned to the laptops' device group
why: Hybrid join through Autopilot needs the Intune Connector for Active Directory to create the computer object on-premises, and a Domain Join profile that tells it which domain and OU to use. Self-deploying profiles support Microsoft Entra join only, device preparation also supports only Entra join, and the laptops do not need a pre-created registered record.

q: Front-desk PCs should drop users straight into their Cloud PC at the Windows sign-in screen. Laptop users already signed in to their local desktop should be able to move to their Cloud PC from the taskbar without signing out. Which pairing of capabilities fits, respectively?
opts: Windows 365 Boot for the front-desk PCs and for the laptops
Windows 365 Frontline (now Windows 365 Flex) for the front-desk PCs; Windows 365 Switch for the laptops
Windows 365 Boot for the front-desk PCs; Windows 365 Switch for the laptops
Windows 365 Switch for the front-desk PCs; Windows 365 Boot for the laptops
why: Windows 365 Boot changes how a session starts, signing the user in at the lock screen straight into the Cloud PC, which matches the front desk. Windows 365 Switch moves a user between the local desktop and the Cloud PC from within a signed-in session, which matches the laptops. Reversing them swaps the two behaviors, Frontline is a licensing model rather than a sign-in experience, and Boot alone would not give laptop users a way to move back and forth without signing out.

q: Autopilot Reset removes a device's Microsoft Entra join and Intune enrollment, so the device must go through full enrollment again at the next out-of-box experience.
opts: True
False
why: Autopilot Reset wipes personal data, apps, and settings but keeps the device's connection to Microsoft Entra ID and its management connection to Intune, then reapplies provisioning. That is why it is the fast way to reissue a device without repeating enrollment.

q: Contoso uses user-driven Autopilot with Microsoft Entra join. Help desk wants every laptop named with the prefix LT- followed by the serial number. Serial numbers are never longer than 12 characters. What should the admin do?
opts: LT-%SERIAL%-%RAND:6% so that every name is guaranteed to be unique
Rename the devices with a platform script after the user first signs in to Windows
A template that fits in 15 characters, such as LT-%SERIAL%
Configure the name in the domain join profile only, since name templates require hybrid join
why: A device name template is limited to 15 characters and supports %SERIAL% and %RAND:x%; it requires Microsoft Entra join. LT- plus a 12-character serial is exactly 15 characters, which fits, while adding a random part would exceed the limit. Hybrid join profiles only accept a prefix. A script after sign-in is unnecessary and renames late in the process.

q: A company needs to deploy new laptops that are hybrid Microsoft Entra joined, with a technician pre-provisioning them at a depot before shipping. Which Autopilot approach should it choose?
opts: Windows Autopilot device preparation in user-driven mode with hybrid join
Windows Autopilot device preparation in automatic mode
A classic Windows Autopilot deployment profile in pre-provisioning mode
A self-deploying profile with the Enrollment Status Page disabled
why: Device preparation supports Microsoft Entra join only, and it has no technician pre-provisioning flow, so a scenario with hybrid join and pre-provisioning needs classic profiles. A self-deploying profile does not include a technician phase and disabling the ESP is not related to the requirement.

q: An admin creates a feature update policy targeting Windows 11. Several Windows 10 laptops in the group do not meet Windows 11 hardware requirements and should still receive the newest Windows 10 feature update. Which approach avoids a second policy?
opts: Wait for each ineligible device to be dropped from the group automatically by Intune
Edit the existing policy later to add the Windows 10 fallback once the first deployment completes
Select the option to install the latest Windows 10 feature update on devices not capable of Windows 11
Create a dynamic group of ineligible devices and assign them an update ring with a 0-day deferral
why: The policy option installs the latest Windows 10 feature update on ineligible devices, so one policy covers both groups. The option has to be chosen when the policy is created, because editing it later ends the current deployment and starts two new ones. An update ring deferral does not offer a feature update, and devices are not removed from groups automatically.

q: Contoso wants employees who replace their laptops to see their personalized Windows settings and Microsoft Store app list restored during the out-of-box experience on the new device. New devices use user-driven Autopilot with Microsoft Entra join. What must the admin configure?
opts: Windows settings backup and restore: a backup policy, plus restore enabled for enrollment
A self-deploying Autopilot profile, because it restores user data without any sign-in
A Windows 365 Boot guided scenario for the new laptops, so settings follow the user
Enterprise State Roaming only, configured for each user's device group in Microsoft Entra ID
why: Windows settings backup and restore (formerly Windows Backup for Organizations) is opt-in: admins configure backup policy (backup is on by default only from Windows 11 version 26H2) and enable restore, either in the tenant-wide enrollment setting or a settings catalog policy. OOBE restore requires a user-driven Autopilot profile, so a self-deploying profile does not work. Windows 365 Boot is for connecting to a Cloud PC, and Enterprise State Roaming management has moved into this feature.

q: A warehouse runs Zebra handheld scanners enrolled as Android Enterprise dedicated devices. They need Zebra-specific settings that the standard Android profiles do not expose. What should the admin deploy?
opts: A custom OMA-URI profile that sets Zebra configuration service provider paths
An OEMConfig profile using the Zebra OEMConfig app approved in managed Google Play
A Windows Autopilot deployment profile assigned to the Zebra scanners
An app protection policy that targets the scanner firmware and operating system
why: Manufacturer-specific settings on Android Enterprise devices are delivered with OEMConfig, using the OEM's OEMConfig app (for Zebra, Zebra OEMConfig Powered by MX on newer Android versions). OMA-URI profiles configure Windows CSP settings, Autopilot is for Windows, and app protection policies protect app data, not device firmware.

q: Contractors use their personal, unenrolled iPhones and Android phones. Security wants them to reach an on-premises web app only through a corporate VPN gateway, with Conditional Access still applied, and without enrolling the devices. Which Intune capability fits?
opts: Microsoft Tunnel for MAM, which extends the Tunnel gateway to unenrolled devices
A Wi-Fi configuration profile assigned to the contractors' own personal devices
A SCEP certificate profile deployed to the contractors' phones for VPN sign-in
A device compliance policy that requires enrollment before the VPN can be used
why: Tunnel for MAM extends the existing Microsoft Tunnel gateway to Android and iOS devices that are not enrolled in Intune, through managed apps. Wi-Fi profiles and SCEP certificates need enrolled devices, and a compliance policy that requires enrollment defeats the BYOD goal.

q: A school district must wipe 90 student tablets at the end of term from the Intune admin center without selecting each device one by one. Which approach is appropriate?
opts: The Retire action, because only retire is supported in bulk device actions
Devices > All devices > Bulk device actions, selecting up to 100 devices
A compliance policy with an action that wipes devices automatically on a chosen date
Deleting the Microsoft Entra security group that holds all of the student devices
why: Bulk device actions support up to 100 devices at a time and include wipe. Compliance actions for noncompliance do not wipe on a date, retire is not the only bulk action, and deleting a group does not wipe the devices.

q: During a call a help-desk technician reads a BitLocker recovery key aloud to a user. Security wants that key invalidated immediately, without touching the user's device. What should the admin do?
opts: Wipe the device so that a new key is generated during the next enrollment
Run the BitLocker key rotation action from the device page
Reset the user's password in Microsoft Entra ID so old secrets stop working
Disable BitLocker on the device and then enable it again at a later date
why: The BitLocker key rotation remote action generates a new recovery key for the OS drive and escrows it, so the old key is useless. Wiping or decrypting the device is far more disruptive, and a password reset does not change BitLocker keys.

q: A laptop's built-in administrator password was shared with a vendor during a support session. The device is Entra joined and its Windows LAPS password already backs up to Microsoft Entra ID. What is the quickest way to change the password right now?
opts: Run the Rotate local admin password remote action
Wait for the next scheduled password age to expire under the LAPS policy
Re-enroll the device in Intune so that the account is recreated
Remove the Windows LAPS policy from the device so it generates a new one
why: The rotate local admin password action forces a new password outside the LAPS schedule for corporate-owned Windows devices that already back up to Microsoft Entra ID. Waiting leaves the old password valid, and removing the policy or re-enrolling does not rotate it.

q: Apple ADE devices enroll, but required apps and policies assigned to a dynamic group arrive late because group membership evaluation lags behind setup. The admin wants the device in a security group already during enrollment. Which feature should be used?
opts: Enrollment time grouping in the Apple enrollment policy
A scope tag that is added to the enrollment profile
Device categories that are chosen by the user in the Company Portal
An assignment filter that is applied to the app assignment
why: Enrollment time grouping assigns the device to a specified Microsoft Entra security group during enrollment so group-targeted content applies earlier in setup. Assignment filters narrow a deployment but do not add group membership. Scope tags control admin visibility, and categories rely on the user acting after enrollment.

q: Contoso manages iPads and Macs. It wants all devices to install the newest OS 14 days after release at 02:00, without sending update commands from Intune. Which setup fits?
opts: A settings catalog Declarative Device Management policy: enforce latest, 14 days delay, 02:00 install time
A custom compliance policy that flags devices whose operating system version is behind the newest release
An old MDM-based iOS update policy with a scheduled install window, pushed to the devices by command
An update ring with a 14-day quality update deferral, assigned to the iPads and Macs as for Windows
why: Apple update policies now use Declarative Device Management in the settings catalog: the Latest version model uses a delay in days and an install time, and devices enforce it themselves. The MDM-based update policies are deprecated. Update rings are for Windows, and a compliance policy only reports state.

q: Contoso manages corporate-owned Samsung and Zebra devices in a warehouse and wants firmware updates delivered to devices without user action, scheduled outside shifts. Which approach should the admin use?
opts: A Wi-Fi profile that forces the devices to download the latest firmware
An app protection policy with conditional launch set to the minimum OS version
A Windows feature update deployment profile assigned to the warehouse device group
FOTA updates with the Samsung Knox E-FOTA and Zebra LifeGuard OTA integrations
why: FOTA management is available for corporate-owned Android Enterprise devices through manufacturer integrations (Samsung E-FOTA, Zebra LifeGuard OTA), with scheduling; it needs a license that includes it, such as Intune Plan 2. The other options are Windows update, app-level, or connectivity features and do not control firmware.

q: A technician needs to roll a new compliance policy to a fleet in stages: a pilot ring first, then 25 percent of devices after three days, then everyone. The admin wants a reusable rollout pattern for other payloads too. Which Intune capability is designed for this?
opts: A scope tag created for each ring, applied to the compliance policy
Deployment plans, which define rings with deferral days between them
Device categories with automatic group membership for each ring
Policy sets, which bundle payloads together for a single assignment
why: Deployment plans (currently in public preview) are reusable templates that define rings of group assignments with deferrals between them, applied to an app or policy through a deployment. Policy sets bundle items but do not stage them over time, categories do not time anything, and scope tags only control visibility.

q: Teams reports Windows 11 laptops running very old Microsoft Defender Antivirus definitions after a long outage. The admin wants to refresh the definitions on one device immediately from Intune. Which action should be used?
opts: The Autopilot Reset action on that single device
The Fresh Start action, which reinstalls Windows on that device
The Update Windows Defender security intelligence remote action
The Wipe action, followed by re-enrollment of the device
why: The security intelligence update action tells the device to refresh Microsoft Defender Antivirus definitions immediately. Wipe, Autopilot Reset, and Fresh Start reset or reinstall the device and are not proportionate.

q: Windows 365 admins want new Cloud PCs for developers to start from a preconfigured image that already contains Microsoft 365 Apps and Teams optimizations, with no image building. Where should they get it?
opts: A generation 1 image with a recovery partition
The gallery images offered when creating the provisioning policy
A custom image captured from a multi-session Azure Virtual Desktop host
An image that contains FSLogix profile containers pre-installed
why: The Windows 365 gallery offers images with Microsoft 365 Apps preinstalled (and Teams optimizations) that are updated monthly, so no custom image is needed. Custom images cannot be multi-session, cannot contain FSLogix components, must not have a recovery partition, and new ones must be generation 2.

q: Windows Autopilot device preparation can hybrid Microsoft Entra join a device.
opts: True
False
why: Device preparation supports Microsoft Entra join only. Hybrid join requires a classic Autopilot deployment profile together with the domain join configuration.

q: Windows settings backup and restore requires admins to configure backup policy, because backup is not turned on automatically on Windows 11 versions earlier than 26H2.
opts: True
False
why: The feature is opt-in until an admin configures it; Windows 11 version 26H2 changes the default so backup is enabled by default on eligible devices, but admin-set policy is still honored and restore still has to be configured.

q: Which two statements about Intune remote actions are accurate? (Choose two.)
opts: Rotate local admin password works only when Windows LAPS is already backing the password up to Microsoft Entra ID for Windows devices
BitLocker key rotation is supported on iOS/iPadOS devices
Bulk device actions can run on up to 100 devices at a time
Bulk wipes do not count toward the daily tenant limit for the wipe action
why: Bulk actions cap at 100 devices and rotating the local admin password for Windows requires that Windows LAPS backs up to Microsoft Entra ID. BitLocker key rotation applies to Windows, and bulk wipe, retire, and delete requests do count toward the daily limits.

q: Which two statements about Microsoft Tunnel and Tunnel for MAM are accurate? (Choose two.)
opts: Tunnel for MAM on iOS/iPadOS provides device-wide VPN
Tunnel for MAM requires an existing Microsoft Tunnel gateway
Tunnel for MAM supports devices that are not enrolled in Intune
Tunnel for MAM replaces the Microsoft Tunnel gateway
why: Tunnel for MAM extends an existing Tunnel gateway to unenrolled devices. It does not replace the gateway, and on iOS/iPadOS it is per-app through the SDK, not device-wide.

q: New Windows laptops sign in with work accounts and join Microsoft Entra ID successfully, but none ever appear in Intune. All users are licensed, and no enrollment restriction blocks Windows. Which setting should the admin check first?
opts: The MAM user scope for Microsoft Intune under Microsoft Entra Mobility (MDM and MAM)
The Entra device setting that limits how many devices each user can join
The tenant-wide compliance setting for devices with no compliance policy assigned
The MDM user scope for Microsoft Intune under Microsoft Entra Mobility (MDM and MAM)
why: The MDM user scope decides whose devices are enrolled in Intune automatically when they join Microsoft Entra ID. If it is set to None, or to a group that excludes these users, the join succeeds but no enrollment happens. The MAM user scope only affects app protection on unenrolled devices. A per-user device limit in Entra would block the join itself, which the stem says succeeds, and the no-policy compliance setting changes how compliance is reported, not whether a device enrolls.

q: Contoso's default enrollment restriction blocks personally owned Windows devices. A higher-priority restriction that allows personal Windows devices is assigned to a group containing the IT team's laptops, yet IT staff still cannot enroll personal devices. What should be changed?
opts: Add a device limit restriction for the group that holds the IT team's laptops
Replace the platform restriction with a compliance policy that blocks personal Windows devices
Assign the allowing restriction to a user group that contains the IT staff
Move the allowing restriction below the default restriction in priority
why: Enrollment restrictions are evaluated for the user who is enrolling, so they must be assigned to user groups. Assigning one to a group of devices means it never applies at enrollment. Priority is already higher than the default, and lowering it would reverse the intent. A device limit caps the number of devices rather than the ownership type, and a compliance policy only acts after enrollment, so it cannot block enrollment.

q: Contoso is retiring on-premises GPOs and moving Windows 11 devices to Intune. The admin wants to learn which GPO settings have MDM equivalents and generate Intune policy from the ones that do, with minimal manual work. What should the admin use?
opts: A security baseline, which imports the existing GPOs and mirrors their settings across the Windows 11 devices
Group Policy analytics, migrating supported settings from an imported GPO into a settings catalog profile
The Administrative templates profile type, with the admin recreating each GPO setting manually in the profile
A custom OMA-URI profile that the admin builds by hand from each setting's ADMX file, one setting at a time
why: Group Policy analytics analyzes an exported GPO, reports which settings have MDM support, and can migrate the supported ones into a settings catalog profile, which removes most of the manual work. A hand-built OMA-URI profile and recreating settings in Administrative templates both do that work by hand, and a security baseline is a Microsoft-defined set of recommended values that does not read your existing GPOs.

q: Domain-joined Windows 11 desktops must become hybrid Microsoft Entra joined so Conditional Access can evaluate them. The admin runs the Microsoft Entra Connect wizard and selects the hybrid join option. What does this configure so the desktops can find the tenant and register themselves?
opts: A service connection point in AD that points the desktops to the tenant
The Intune Connector for Active Directory on a domain-joined server in the forest
A Group Policy setting for automatic MDM enrollment into Intune for the desktops
An Autopilot hybrid join profile assigned to the desktops' device group
why: For hybrid join, Microsoft Entra Connect publishes a service connection point in Active Directory that tells domain-joined Windows devices which tenant to register with, and they then register themselves. Automatic MDM enrollment through Group Policy is a later step that depends on hybrid join already working. The Intune Connector for Active Directory supports Autopilot by creating computer objects for new devices, and an Autopilot profile applies to new or reset devices rather than desktops that are already domain-joined.

q: A user holds Microsoft 365 E3 and has just been assigned a Windows 365 Enterprise license. The user does not belong to any group that Cloud PC provisioning targets. What is the result?
opts: A Cloud PC is created automatically with default settings, as happens for Windows 365 Business licenses
No Cloud PC is created until the user belongs to a group assigned to a provisioning policy
A Cloud PC is created once an admin also assigns the user a separate Intune device license
A Cloud PC is created the first time the user signs in to the Windows 365 portal
why: In Windows 365 Enterprise, a Cloud PC is created only when the user both holds a Windows 365 license and falls inside a group assigned to a provisioning policy. Automatic provisioning on license assignment describes Windows 365 Business, not Enterprise. Microsoft 365 E3 already includes Intune, so no extra Intune license is needed, and a portal sign-in does not trigger creation.

q: Berlin helpdesk admins must see only Berlin's policies and apps, and may run remote actions only on devices of Berlin users. Which settings on their Intune role assignment satisfy both requirements?
opts: Scope (Groups) containing Berlin users and devices, which also hides other regions' policies and apps from the admin
An assignment filter on each Berlin policy, which restricts what administrators can see in the admin center
A Berlin scope tag on the role assignment, which also limits which devices the admin can target with remote actions
A Berlin scope tag for object visibility, plus Scope (Groups) containing Berlin users and devices for what they can target
why: A role assignment has two separate limits: scope tags control which Intune objects an admin can see, and Scope (Groups) controls which users and devices the admin can act on. The scenario needs both, so using only one leaves either the visibility or the targeting wide open. Assignment filters narrow which devices receive an assigned item and have no effect on what an administrator can see.

q: In the Intune admin center the Intune Connector for Active Directory shows as active, yet user-driven hybrid Autopilot devices fail at domain join and no device accounts appear in AD. What should the admin verify first?
opts: That a compliance policy is assigned to the devices before they begin their provisioning run
That each device's hardware hash was registered with the correct group tag before it shipped
That the Enrollment Status Page timeout is long enough for the domain join step to complete
That the connector's account can create computer objects in the Domain Join profile's OU
why: The connector creates the computer object in the OU named in the Domain Join profile, so it needs permission to create computer objects there. An active status does not prove that permission exists. A short ESP timeout would fail later in provisioning, a wrong group tag would stop the profile from assigning before the domain-join stage, and compliance policies are not evaluated before provisioning.

q: A configuration profile is assigned to All devices. IT wants it to skip Windows 10 devices, without creating or maintaining any new groups and while keeping the All devices assignment. What should be added?
opts: An excluded Entra user group that contains the owners of the Windows 10 devices
A dynamic device group for Windows 11 that replaces the All devices assignment
An assignment filter in include mode that matches the Windows 11 OS version range
A scope tag that is applied to the Windows 11 devices
why: An assignment filter evaluates device properties such as OS version on top of the existing assignment, so All devices stays in place and no group is needed. Intune does not evaluate a user-group exclusion against a device-targeted assignment, a scope tag only limits which admins can see an object, and a dynamic device group would work but breaks the stated constraints by adding a group and replacing the assignment.

q: A custom OMA-URI profile is the preferred way to configure a newly released Windows setting, ahead of the settings catalog.
opts: True
False
why: The settings catalog exposes CSP-backed settings individually and is kept current, so it is the first place to look. A custom OMA-URI profile is a fallback for a setting the catalog or a template does not expose.

q: If a user belongs to groups targeted by several enrollment restrictions of the same type, Intune applies only the highest-priority one rather than combining them.
opts: True
False
why: Restrictions of the same type are not merged. The user gets the one with the highest priority among those assigned to their groups, and the built-in default restriction applies only when no assigned restriction covers them.

q: Contoso's Cloud PCs must be hybrid Microsoft Entra joined so users can reach on-premises file shares and apply domain policy. Which provisioning policy configuration is required?
opts: A Microsoft Entra join policy that Intune enrollment later converts into hybrid join
A hybrid join policy that uses an Azure network connection with domain join details
A Microsoft Entra join policy that uses the Microsoft-hosted network and the default image
A hybrid join policy that uses the Microsoft-hosted network with domain join details
why: Hybrid Entra joined Cloud PCs need an Azure network connection that can reach a domain controller and carries the domain join settings. The Microsoft-hosted network supports Microsoft Entra join only, so it cannot be paired with hybrid join, and enrolling a Cloud PC in Intune does not convert its join type.

q: Which two statements about Microsoft Entra device states are accurate? (Choose two.)
opts: A Microsoft Entra registered device signs users in to Windows with their Entra credentials at the sign-in screen
A Microsoft Entra registered device is typically personal, with a work account added and no organizational control of sign-in
A hybrid Microsoft Entra joined device has an on-premises AD computer account and is also known to Entra ID
Hybrid Entra join is the only device state that can be enrolled in Intune, since joined devices cannot enroll
A Microsoft Entra joined device must also have a computer object in on-premises Active Directory to authenticate
why: Hybrid joined devices carry both an AD computer account and an Entra ID device object, and registered devices are typically personal ones where a work account has been added without the organization owning the sign-in. An Entra joined device has no on-premises AD account, Intune can enroll joined, hybrid joined, and registered devices, and signing in to Windows with Entra credentials describes a joined device, not a registered one.

q: Configuration Manager devices have been uploaded to the Intune admin center with tenant attach. Security now wants Conditional Access to require a compliant device for them, using Intune compliance policies. What must be done?
opts: Move the Endpoint Protection workload to Intune, since it evaluates device health
Move the Resource access policies workload to Intune, since it holds the compliance settings
Enable co-management and move the Compliance policies workload to Intune
Nothing more, because tenant attach already reports Intune compliance for the uploaded devices
why: Tenant attach only provides visibility and a few remote actions; it neither enrolls the devices nor makes Intune evaluate compliance. To have Intune compliance policies drive Conditional Access, the devices need co-management with the Compliance policies workload set to Intune. Resource access policies covers items such as VPN, Wi-Fi, and certificate profiles, and Endpoint Protection covers security settings, not compliance evaluation.

q: Which two requirements point to Windows 365 rather than Azure Virtual Desktop? (Choose two.)
opts: Microsoft operating the underlying hosting, so no host pools or scaling plans need to be built
Multi-session Windows 11 hosts shared by many users to lower the cost per user
Pay-as-you-go billing for only the compute and storage that is consumed
Scaling session hosts down to zero outside business hours to cut compute spend
A predictable per-user monthly price regardless of how many hours the desktop is used
why: Windows 365 is a fixed-price, per-user Cloud PC whose hosting Microsoft operates. Azure Virtual Desktop is the opposite on each of the other points: it offers multi-session hosts, scaling plans that shut hosts down when idle, and consumption-based billing, all of which the organization configures and manages itself in Azure.

q: An app assigned to a dynamic device group can install later than expected on a freshly provisioned device, because group membership is not evaluated instantly.
opts: True
False
why: Dynamic membership is evaluated on a delay, so a new device may briefly sit outside its intended group. For anything that must apply at the moment of provisioning, target an assigned group, or make sure the group tag is set before the device ships.

q: Contoso has 800 Windows 11 laptops that are already enrolled in Intune but were never registered for Autopilot. IT wants them to use a user-driven Autopilot deployment profile the next time they are reset, without collecting hardware hashes device by device. What should IT configure?
opts: Turn on Convert all targeted devices to Autopilot in the deployment profile assigned to the laptops
Assign a dynamic device group built on a group tag to the deployment profile for the laptops
Ask the OEM to retroactively register each laptop's serial number through its partner portal account
Run a hardware hash export script on each laptop and import the combined CSV files into Intune
why: A deployment profile can convert the Intune-managed devices it targets into Autopilot devices, which registers them without collecting hashes manually. Retroactive OEM registration is slow and depends on purchase records, a hash export script is exactly the per-device collection the scenario wants to avoid, and a group tag cannot be matched on devices that were never registered and so have no tag.

q: A global company wants regional IT admins to manage only their own region's Intune devices and policies within one tenant, and regional HR admins to manage only their own region's Entra ID user accounts and licensing in that same tenant. Which pairing fits each need respectively?
opts: Scope tags with scoped role assignments for Intune delegation; administrative units for Entra ID user and license delegation
Administrative units for Intune delegation; scope tags for Entra ID user and license delegation
Scope (Groups) on the Intune role assignments for both needs, since it also limits which Entra users an admin can manage
A dynamic device group per region for Intune delegation; a Conditional Access policy per region for Entra licensing
why: Scope tags with scoped role assignments are Intune's own delegation mechanism for devices and policies, while administrative units are the Entra ID mechanism for scoping user and license administration. Swapping them applies each tool to the wrong directory. Scope (Groups) works inside Intune and does not extend to Entra user administration, and device groups and Conditional Access do not delegate administrative rights at all.

q: An admin tries to enroll new iPads through Automated Device Enrollment, but every attempt fails. At the same time, iPhones already managed by Intune have stopped receiving MDM commands. What is the most likely cause?
opts: The Apple Push Notification service (APNs) certificate has expired and must be renewed under the original Apple ID
The VPP token that Intune uses for app licensing has expired and must be renewed in the admin center
The Apple Business Manager server token used for Automated Device Enrollment has expired and needs renewing
A platform enrollment restriction is blocking iOS/iPadOS enrollment for the users in the tenant
why: An expired APNs certificate stops Intune from pushing MDM commands to every enrolled Apple device and blocks new Apple enrollment at the same time, which matches both symptoms. An expired Automated Device Enrollment token would break new ADE enrollment and sync but not commands to enrolled iPhones, an expired VPP token affects only app licensing, and an enrollment restriction blocks new enrollments without touching devices that are already managed.

q: Regional HR admins must be able to reset passwords for users in their own region only, and must have no Intune permissions at all. What should be configured?
opts: Scope (Groups) on an Intune role assignment that lists each region's user group
The Password Administrator role assigned at tenant scope, with a Conditional Access policy limiting which users it covers
A scope tag per region, with the Intune Help Desk Operator role assigned to the HR admins at that tag
An administrative unit per region holding that region's users, with the Password Administrator role scoped to it
why: An administrative unit scopes a directory role such as Password Administrator to only the users inside it, which is directory-level delegation with no Intune rights implied. A scope tag with an Intune role does the opposite, granting Intune permissions and limiting only Intune objects. A tenant-scoped role covers every user, and Conditional Access cannot narrow an administrator's role. Scope (Groups) exists only on Intune role assignments.

q: A company deploys certificate-based Wi-Fi to managed Windows laptops. Which two statements are correct? (Choose two.)
opts: The SCEP certificate profile references a trusted certificate profile that delivers the root CA to the devices
A Wi-Fi profile that uses EAP-TLS issues the device's client certificate by itself during connection
The Wi-Fi profile references the certificate profile that supplies the client certificate used to authenticate
The trusted certificate profile can be skipped because Windows trusts the CA behind an installed client certificate
Certificate-based Wi-Fi works with Microsoft Cloud PKI as the issuer but not with SCEP or PKCS certificates
why: A SCEP profile points at a trusted certificate profile for the root CA, and the Wi-Fi profile points at the certificate profile to use for client authentication, so the pieces must be assigned together. A Wi-Fi profile does not issue certificates, Windows does not automatically trust the issuing CA without the root being delivered, and SCEP, PKCS, and Cloud PKI can all supply the certificate.

q: Contoso blocks personally owned iOS devices with a platform enrollment restriction. Procurement bought 50 iPhones at retail that must enroll as corporate-owned anyway. Which setting lets them enroll?
opts: Raise the device limit restriction for the users who will receive them
Add a higher-priority platform restriction that allows personal iOS devices for those users
Assign a Corporate device category to the 50 iPhones before they enroll
Upload their serial numbers as corporate device identifiers
why: Corporate device identifiers mark specific hardware, by serial number or IMEI, as corporate-owned at enrollment, so the personal-device block does not apply and the ownership value is correct afterward. A device limit restriction counts devices rather than ownership. A higher-priority allow rule would let those users enroll personal devices too and would record the iPhones as personal, and a device category is a purpose label that does not affect ownership or the restriction.

q: Contoso issues Android phones to 300 delivery drivers. The phones are company-owned, each is assigned to one driver, IT wants full control of the whole device, and drivers must not be able to add personal accounts. Which Android Enterprise enrollment option should the admin use?
opts: Personally owned devices with a work profile, so personal and work data stay separate
Corporate-owned dedicated (COSU) devices, because every phone is used for one business purpose
Android device administrator, which gives the broadest control on every Android version
Corporate-owned fully managed (COBO)
why: Fully managed enrollment is for company-owned devices assigned to a user, where Intune manages the whole device. A personal work profile separates data on devices the user owns and leaves the rest of the phone alone. Dedicated devices are user-less kiosks or shared devices, which does not match phones assigned to individual drivers. Device administrator is a legacy mode that offers less control on current Android versions and is not the recommended option.

q: A user reports that her new personal iPhone will not enroll. The enrollment failures report shows reason "device limit reached" for her account. Other users enroll fine. What should the admin check?
opts: Whether the Apple Push Notification service certificate has expired for the whole tenant and every Apple device
Whether the Intune Connector for Active Directory is installed on a domain-joined server
Whether the iPhone has first been registered in Windows Autopilot by its hardware hash
The device limit restriction that applies to her, and how many devices she already has enrolled
why: A device limit restriction caps how many devices one user can enroll; the failure reason in the enrollment failures report points directly at it, so the admin raises the limit or removes an old device. An expired Apple Push Notification certificate would affect every Apple enrollment, not one user. The Active Directory connector concerns hybrid Windows devices, and Autopilot registration is a Windows-only process.

q: A Windows 365 admin must let a colleague view Cloud PC provisioning policies, images, and Cloud PCs in the Intune admin center, but not change anything. Which role fits?
opts: Intune Administrator
Windows 365 Network Interface Contributor
Cloud PC Reader
Cloud PC Administrator
why: Cloud PC Reader is a built-in read-only role for the Windows 365 node. Cloud PC Administrator manages images, network connections, and provisioning, which means it can change things. The Windows 365 Network Interface Contributor role is a role the Windows 365 service receives on the Azure network connection's resource group, not an admin role. Intune Administrator is far broader than needed.

q: A small consultancy's Cloud PCs only need internet access and Microsoft 365 apps. The admin has no Azure subscription or virtual network and wants nothing to build or maintain for networking. Which provisioning configuration fits?
opts: An Azure network connection with Microsoft Entra join, using a virtual network the admin builds in Azure
The Microsoft-hosted network with Microsoft Entra join
An Azure network connection with hybrid Microsoft Entra join, using an existing on-premises domain
A gallery image with Microsoft 365 Apps preinstalled, which also supplies the network connection
why: The Microsoft-hosted network is operated by Microsoft, needs no Azure subscription or virtual network, and supports Microsoft Entra join, which is enough when Cloud PCs only need internet and cloud apps. An Azure network connection means building and maintaining a virtual network, with its health checks and roles, and is justified by on-premises access or hybrid join, so both Azure network connection options add work the admin wants to avoid. The image content has no effect on networking.

q: A security review of an Intune tenant finds that new Windows devices can be used by employees without ever being enrolled. The auditors reference Zero Trust recommendations. Which tenant setting addresses this?
opts: Add scope tags to every device configuration profile in the tenant
Create a compliance policy that is assigned only to the Android devices
Turn on enrollment notifications that are sent only to administrators
Enforce Windows automatic enrollment so devices joining Entra ID enroll
why: Automatic MDM enrollment makes Windows devices that join Microsoft Entra ID enroll in Intune, so unmanaged endpoints are not left outside management and compliance. Notifications and scope tags help awareness and delegation but do not enroll anything. An Android-only compliance policy does not touch Windows devices.

q: Which two statements about Windows 365 Cloud PC provisioning are accurate? (Choose two.)
opts: The Microsoft-hosted network can reach on-premises Active Directory directly
A Cloud PC needs an Azure network connection to be hybrid Microsoft Entra joined
A custom image can be a multi-session image
A custom image must be generation 2 and generalized
why: Custom images must be generation 2, generalized, single-session images, and hybrid join requires an Azure network connection. Multi-session images are not supported, and the Microsoft-hosted network has no line of sight to on-premises Active Directory.

q: Conditional Access requires a compliant device for Exchange Online. Auditors found that a newly enrolled laptop, which has not yet received any compliance policy, can still open mail. Which tenant-wide Intune setting should change?
opts: Set the Mark device noncompliant action to 0 days in every compliance policy
Mark devices with no compliance policy assigned as Not compliant
Shorten the compliance status validity period to one day
Turn on enhanced jailbreak detection for mobile devices
why: By default, a device with no compliance policy assigned is reported as compliant, which is why the new laptop passes the Conditional Access check. Flipping that setting to Not compliant closes the gap. The validity period only affects devices that stop checking in, enhanced jailbreak detection is a mobile setting, and a 0-day noncompliance action lives inside individual policies, which the new laptop has not received.

q: A Conditional Access policy requires a compliant device for Exchange Online. A user signs in from a compliant corporate laptop and from their own noncompliant, Intune-enrolled phone. What happens?
opts: The laptop is blocked as well, because requiring a compliant device also implies a hybrid Microsoft Entra joined device
Both are granted, because the policy is satisfied once one of the user's devices is compliant
The laptop gets access and the phone is blocked, because compliance is evaluated for the specific device used at each sign-in
Both are blocked until the phone is remediated, because compliance follows the user across their registered devices
why: The require device to be marked as compliant grant control is device-bound, so it checks the device used for that particular sign-in. The compliant laptop passes and the noncompliant phone is blocked. Compliance is not pooled across a user's devices in either direction, and hybrid join is a different grant control that this policy does not include.

q: Security wants Windows devices that Microsoft Defender for Endpoint rates as high risk to lose Conditional Access-gated access automatically. The devices are Intune-enrolled but not yet onboarded to Defender for Endpoint. Which step should the admin do first?
opts: Deploy an attack surface reduction policy in audit mode to the Windows devices
Turn on the Intune connection to Defender for Endpoint in the admin center
Add a machine risk score requirement to the Windows compliance policy for the laptops
Create the Conditional Access policy that requires a compliant device for Exchange Online
why: The connection between Intune and Defender for Endpoint comes first because it lets Intune deploy the onboarding configuration and receive each device's risk signal. The machine risk rule in the compliance policy and the Conditional Access policy that consumes the result build on top of that connection and onboarding. An attack surface reduction policy in audit mode neither onboards devices nor feeds compliance.

q: A security baseline profile was assigned to a device group a year ago. Microsoft has since released a newer baseline version, but devices still enforce the old settings. IT wants the new defaults without recreating the profile or its assignments. What should IT do?
opts: Create a new profile from the newer baseline, since existing instances stay locked to their original version
Wait for the next device check-in, when assigned baselines update to the latest version automatically
Remove and re-add the devices to the assigned group so that the baseline is re-evaluated
Move the existing profile instance to the newer baseline version, then review its settings
why: Baselines are versioned, and an existing profile instance picks up a newer version only when an admin moves it to that version, which keeps its assignments in place. Nothing updates automatically at check-in, a new profile is not required because instances can be moved, and changing group membership has no effect on which baseline version the profile uses.

q: A help desk technician reads a BitLocker recovery key aloud to a user during a call. Security now wants each key to become invalid once it has been used for recovery, with no technician action afterward. Keys are already escrowed to Microsoft Entra ID. What should be added?
opts: A Rotate BitLocker keys remote action, run by a technician after each recovery call
Client-driven recovery password rotation, enabled in the disk encryption policy
A compliance policy that requires BitLocker and regenerates the key at its next evaluation
A Wipe action sent to each device after its recovery key has been used
why: Client-driven recovery password rotation makes the device generate a new recovery password and escrow it after the old one is used, which needs no one to act afterward. The Rotate BitLocker keys remote action also works but depends on a technician remembering to run it. Wiping the device destroys data to solve a key problem, and compliance policies check for BitLocker without regenerating keys.

q: Developers must run one IT-approved installer that needs administrator rights every time it runs. Security wants administrator rights limited to that installer, a typed reason from the developer each time, and no developer added to the local Administrators group. What should be configured?
opts: An Endpoint Privilege Management elevation rule for that file, with user-confirmed elevation and required justification
A Win32 app deployment that reinstalls the tool under the SYSTEM account whenever the developers need to run it
A local user group membership policy that adds the developers to the Administrators group on their laptops
A Windows LAPS policy that lets the developers retrieve the rotated local administrator password for each device
why: An Endpoint Privilege Management rule elevates only the specific approved file, and the user-confirmed type can require a business justification, with no change to group membership. LAPS would hand developers a full administrator credential, adding them to the Administrators group is exactly what security forbids, and reinstalling the tool does not help when the program needs elevation each time it runs.

q: A Conditional Access policy that requires a compliant device for all cloud apps should keep the Microsoft Intune Enrollment cloud app included, so that only already-compliant devices can enroll.
opts: True
False
why: A device cannot be compliant before it has enrolled, so including the Microsoft Intune Enrollment cloud app creates a catch-22 that blocks new enrollments. It should be excluded from the compliance requirement.

q: By default, a user can view the BitLocker recovery key of their own Microsoft Entra joined device in the My Account portal.
opts: True
False
why: This sounds risky but is the default: the Entra device setting that restricts users from recovering their own BitLocker keys is off. An admin can turn it on when keys should only be released by the help desk.

q: Which two statements about Endpoint Privilege Management elevation rules are accurate? (Choose two.)
opts: A rule can require the user to enter a business justification before elevation proceeds
A rule adds the user to the local Administrators group for the rest of the session
Rules apply to any Microsoft Entra registered device, including personal phones
A rule can target a specific file by its hash or its signing certificate
A rule removes the need for the device to be managed by Intune
why: Elevation rules identify an approved file by attributes such as its hash or certificate, and they can require a justification before elevating. A rule elevates only that application and never changes group membership, and it works on Intune-managed Windows devices rather than registered personal phones or unmanaged machines.

q: Which two statements about compliance policies and Conditional Access are accurate? (Choose two.)
opts: Compliance results reach Conditional Access only for corporate-owned devices, not personal ones
An unenrolled phone cannot satisfy the require compliant device control, because Intune holds no state for it
A device that does not check in within the compliance status validity period is treated as noncompliant
A device that passes one assigned compliance policy is compliant even if it fails another assigned policy
A compliance policy blocks sign-in on its own, with no Conditional Access policy required
why: Devices that stop reporting are treated as noncompliant once the validity period passes, and a device Intune does not manage has no compliance state to present. A device must meet every assigned policy, compliance by itself only records a status and Conditional Access is what blocks sign-in, and enrolled personal devices do report compliance to Conditional Access.

q: Contoso wants to eliminate password sign-in on managed Windows laptops. Each user should unlock with a PIN or biometric backed by a key stored in that laptop's TPM, not by a portable token. What should be deployed through Intune?
opts: Microsoft Authenticator passwordless phone sign-in registered for each user's phone
FIDO2 security keys registered to each user's account and carried between devices
Windows Hello for Business, deployed through a device configuration or settings catalog profile
A compliance policy that requires a strong password and a short lock timeout on the laptops
why: Windows Hello for Business replaces the password with a PIN or biometric that unlocks a key pair bound to that device's TPM, and it is deployed through an Intune profile. A FIDO2 security key is a portable token rather than a per-laptop key. Authenticator phone sign-in is a different passwordless method that does not unlock Windows with a device-bound key, and a compliance policy only checks password requirements instead of replacing the credential.

q: A Windows LAPS policy backs up local administrator passwords to Microsoft Entra ID, and the passwords are rotating on the laptops. Yet technicians with the Cloud Device Administrator role see no password for any device. What is the most likely missing step?
opts: Enabling the LAPS setting in the tenant's Microsoft Entra device settings
Adding the technicians to the local Administrators group on each laptop they support
Assigning an Endpoint Privilege Management elevation rule to the technicians' accounts
Changing the policy's backup directory from Entra ID to on-premises Active Directory
why: Microsoft Entra only accepts backed-up LAPS passwords when the LAPS setting is turned on in the tenant's device settings, so a deployed policy can rotate passwords locally yet have nothing to show in Entra. Technicians read the password from the directory and do not need local group membership. On-premises AD is a different backup target, and Endpoint Privilege Management elevates applications rather than exposing passwords.

q: A line-of-business server app needs inbound TCP 8443 opened on Windows laptops, but only while a laptop is on the corporate domain network. Which Intune policy fits?
opts: A VPN profile that forwards port 8443 traffic from the corporate network to the laptops
An attack surface reduction rule that permits network connections on port 8443 from the laptops
A Microsoft Defender Firewall rules policy with an inbound allow rule for port 8443 on the Domain profile
A Microsoft Defender Firewall policy that sets the Domain profile's default inbound action to Allow for the laptops
why: A firewall rules policy can define one inbound allow rule for a specific port and bind it to the Domain profile, so it opens only that port, only on the corporate network. Setting the Domain profile's default inbound action to Allow opens every port, which is far broader than needed. ASR rules do not manage firewall ports, and a VPN profile configures a tunnel rather than inbound firewall rules.

q: A compliance policy marks devices noncompliant after a 5-day grace period. Security wants the user emailed the moment the device first fails a setting, and again on day 3, with no other change to the policy. What should the admin configure?
opts: A notification setting inside a device configuration profile assigned to the same users
A shorter grace period on the Mark device noncompliant action, set to 0 days
Two Send email to end user actions on the policy, scheduled at 0 days and 3 days
A Conditional Access policy that emails the user when a sign-in is blocked
why: A compliance policy accepts several noncompliance actions, each with its own schedule, so one email action at 0 days and another at 3 days run alongside the 5-day mark-noncompliant action, each using a notification message template. Conditional Access reacts at sign-in rather than when a setting fails, configuration profiles carry no compliance notifications, and a 0-day grace period would change when the device is marked noncompliant, which the scenario says to leave alone.

q: A team wants standard users to run one IT-approved application that needs administrator rights, without ever granting standing local administrator access, and also wants help desk to look up a fallback local administrator password for the same machine in an emergency. Which pairing satisfies both needs without contradiction?
opts: A local user group membership policy that adds the user to Administrators; Windows LAPS for the fallback password
Windows LAPS for the approved application, handing the user the rotated password only while the installer runs
Endpoint Privilege Management for both needs, since an elevation rule can also escrow a rotated local administrator password
Endpoint Privilege Management for the one approved application; Windows LAPS for the rotated local administrator password
why: Endpoint Privilege Management elevates only the one approved application with no standing admin rights, and Windows LAPS independently manages the rotated local administrator password for emergency use, so the two are complementary. LAPS does not elevate applications for users, Endpoint Privilege Management does not manage or escrow the local administrator password, and putting the user in Administrators creates exactly the standing access the team wants to avoid.
